title: Proxied LLM stream fragmentation and resume notes
content:
Context / why I'm writing this
- Running into edge cases when clients go through an HTTP proxy/load-balancer that enforces idle timeouts or chunk coalescing.
- Need a pragmatic resume strategy for server-initiated chunking (server sends partial tokens) where the client may lose the TCP connection mid-stream but still wants to receive the remaining tokens without re-running expensive model work.
- Goal: define API shape + proxy-compatible wire semantics + lightweight checkpoint format that can be persisted client-side or proxied via Redis/kv for resume.

High-level constraints / non-goals\- Minimal changes to existing streaming API (keep same endpoints if possible).\- No heavyweight per-request durable storage on host by default. Resume should be optional and negotiated via headers.\- Avoid leaking internal model state (no raw KV-cache dumps to clients).\- Support resuming across short interruptions (seconds -> minutes). Not targeting multi-hour offline continuation yet.

Definitions (informal)
- fragment: a single contiguous chunk of streamed tokens emitted by server (not necessarily aligned to sentence boundaries).
- checkpoint: a small metadata blob describing state needed to resume from a fragment boundary.
- resume-token: opaque string the client can present to the server (or proxy) to request continuation from the last checkpoint.

API proposal (lightweight)
1) Start stream (unchanged): POST /v1/generate-stream\- headers: Authorization, Content-Type: application/json\- body: {model, prompt, max_tokens, stream: true, resume: optional enum}
  - resume: "off" | "client" | "proxy" | "server"
    - off: default (no resume support)
    - client: server emits resume-tokens to client, client stores locally and can re-open to server if interrupted
    - proxy: server emits resume-tokens meant for an intermediate proxy or gateway that can hold checkpoint state for N seconds
    - server: server persists checkpoint for configured TTL (heavier)

2) Streaming frames (existing SSE / chunked-encoding) - augmented semantics\- Normal token frame: {"type":"token","token":"...","seq":123} (unchanged)\- Checkpoint frame (periodic, every N tokens / at sentence boundaries):
    {"type":"checkpoint","seq":123,"resume_token":"r:TOKEN","checkpoint_ttl":30}
  - resume_token: opaque base64 (server-signed, short)
  - checkpoint_ttl: seconds server will hold state if server-mode; hint for proxies/clients for cache expiry

3) Resume flow (client-side)
- Client reconnects and POSTs /v1/generate-resume with header: Authorization and body: {"resume_token":"r:TOKEN"}
- Server validates resume_token, rehydrates minimal state (attention prefix summary + last-k tokens checksum) and continues streaming new tokens starting at seq+1.
- If server cannot resume (expired/invalid), respond 410/Gone with structured body {"error":"resume_expired","reason":"checkpoint ttl exceeded"} or 400 if token malformed.

4) Proxy flow
- If resume=proxy, the resume_token is scoped to proxy and contains an identifier like r:proxy:v1:uuid
- Proxy is expected to store checkpoint blob (opaque value from server) in its cache keyed by uuid for checkpoint_ttl seconds.
- On client reconnect, proxy intercepts /v1/generate-resume and forwards resume request to origin with proxy-auth header carrying the uuid. Origin validates proxy's token and continues.

Resume-token contents (server-signed opaque string) - NOT client-readable
- Fields encoded inside token (server-only): model-id, seq, partial-output-hash, short HMAC and TTL epoch
- Example (pseudo): base64url(json) + '.' + signature

Checkpoint payload (persisted by server/proxy) - small summary only
- {model: "gpt-like-3b", prompt_hash: "sha256:...", seq: 124, last_k_tokens_hash: "sha256:...", partial_kv_seed: "seed-32"} (server stores this locally, proxy stores opaque blob)
- Note: partial_kv_seed is an internal handle that authorizes the serving host to reconstitute necessary prefix cache — not raw KV state.

Wire-level considerations (proxies & chunking)
- Many proxies coalesce small chunks into larger ones. That is OK: resume-token must be emitted in a single checkpoint frame; use SSE style or ".\n\n" boundary that proxies keep.
- For chunked-encoding over HTTP/1.1, ensure frame boundaries include explicit length markers for checkpoint frames (we can't rely on CRLF boundaries).
- SSE (recommended) keeps events separate; we should prefer SSE for resume semantics. If we keep chunked, include JSON frames prefixed with length integer (framing).

Sequence diagram (ASCII)
Client       Proxy        Origin
  |-----------|------------|
  | POST /generate-stream  |
  |----------------------->|
  |                       -->|  server starts streaming tokens
  |                       <-- chunk(token)
  |      chunk(token)      |
  |<-----------------------|
  |  ... intermittent loss (TCP close) ...  |
  |<-- reconnect with resume token --|
  |---> /generate-resume + r:TOKEN -->|
  |                 proxy fetches checkpoint and forwards -->|
  |                 origin validates and resumes stream -->|

Failure modes and heuristics\- Resume token expired: client should fall back to starting a fresh request with same prompt and use deduping heuristics client-side (e.g., send last N tokens as context and request tokens starting from there).\- Divergence: if prompt had non-determinism (sampling) original continuation may differ; we can only guarantee continuation for deterministic/greedy generation or when server snapshots RNG state (not desirable). Document expectation: resume best-effort, not deterministic for stochastic sampling.

Security / privacy\- Resume tokens must be HMAC-signed with server key and short lived.\- Do not include PII in checkpoint blob that proxies persist. Proxy-mode blob should be opaque and unreadable by proxy (server signs and encrypts the payload). If proxy is customer-managed, we must surface that it is holding opaque bytes and warn customer.

Operational notes\- Emit checkpoint frames at configurable rate: default every 20 tokens or at sentence boundary, whichever sooner.\- TTL default: 30s for proxy-mode, 120s for server-mode (configurable per route).\- Metrics to add: resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, avg_time-to-resume, expired_resume_count, checkpoint_bytes_emitted.

Experiment plan (small steps)
1) Implement server-side resume token generation and checkpoint emission behind feature flag. Keep token opaque and TTL 30s. No proxy semantics yet.\2) Add /v1/generate-resume endpoint and basic validation. Track metrics.\3) Open experiment with a controlled internal proxy (dev infra): enable proxy-mode where proxy stores the blob in Redis and forwards resume requests.\4) Run 2-week heatcheck on a subset of beta customers; measure failures and divergence.

Open questions / TODOs
- Should we support multi-fragment ACKs (client ACKs checkpoint to advance TTL on server/proxy)? Pros: keep state alive for active clients. Cons: adds more messages. Consider optional header "Resume-Ack: seq" from client on keepalive.
- How to handle function-calling / tool outputs mid-stream? If a tool call happened before checkpoint, we need to persist tool-output artifacts or mark resume impossible. Maybe mark resume invalid when non-idempotent external calls happened.
- Long running sessions where the model state size is large: need a different path (session-offload) — out of scope for now.
- CLI debug tools: small tool to decode unsigned fields from token for ops debug (but avoid leaking anything in logs).

Implementation sketch (pseudo code)
- generate_stream(request):
    seq = 0
    for token in model.generate():
       emit({type:"token", token: token, seq: seq})
       if should_emit_checkpoint(seq):
          token = make_resume_token(params)
          emit({type:"checkpoint", seq: seq, resume_token: token, checkpoint_ttl: ttl})
       seq += 1

- resume_flow(resume_token):
    payload = validate_token(resume_token)
    if expired(payload): return 410
    state_handle = lookup_state(payload.handle)
    rehydrate_prefix(state_handle)
    continue generation from payload.seq+1

Notes to self\- Keep tokens small and token frames simple to avoid proxy reassembly bugs.\- Document expected compatibility with common proxies (nginx/gcp-http-proxy/aws-alb) and test with slow clients.\- Add regression test harness that simulates mid-stream drop and resume with varying sampling seeds.

Brainstorm: cheaper client-only resume option\- Client stores last N tokens and attempts to re-request with promptSuffix: lastN and a flag "dedupe_prefix=true" so server attempts to detect duplicate prefix and skip tokens already returned (server computes overlapping-match). Useful when server can't or won't persist anything. This is less precise but low-cost.
